author: Latham, 1801
summary: 서해와 남해의 섬에서 주로 5월에 드물게 관찰되는 길잃은새로, 지금까지 기록이 10건이 안 된다. 사할린과 일본 홋카이도~혼슈 중부에서 번식하고 중국 동부를 거쳐 동남아시아로 내려가 겨울을 난다. 이마에서 눈 뒤까지 넓고 흰 띠가 이어지고 몸 윗면이 선명한 적갈색이어서 다른 노랑때까치 무리와 구별된다.

art.subject: Brown Shrike of the race superciliosus (Lanius cristatus superciliosus), adult male in spring: a broad white band across the forehead continuing back as a long, broad white supercilium; crown, nape, mantle and rump bright chestnut-rufous; a black mask from the bill through the eye to the ear-coverts; wings dark brown with rufous fringes; throat white; underparts white with a warm buff-orange wash on the breast sides and flanks; tail rufous-brown. Bill blackish; dark eye; legs dark grey.
art.pose: perched upright on a bare twig at the top of a shrub, side view
art.scene: Shrubby field edge on a Korean offshore island in May, during spring migration, clear light; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male in spring, side view perched upright on a bare twig: wide white forehead band and broad white supercilium, black mask from the bill to near the nape, bright rufous crown, nape, mantle and rump, dark brown wings with rufous edgings, white throat, pale underparts, longish rufous-brown tail, hooked blackish bill

adult female, side view perched upright on a twig: duller than the male, narrower white forehead band and supercilium, mask less distinct on the lores, rufous-brown upperparts, pale underparts with finely vermiculated flanks
art.build: Medium-small, slim shrike, about the size of Bull-headed Shrike, with a longish, graduated tail. Bill shorter than the head, strong and hooked at the tip. Legs short, dark. Usually no white on the wing; at most a tiny white spot at the base of the primaries. Perches upright on exposed twigs, swinging the tail. Females are duller, with a browner mask and fine dark barring on the flanks.
avoid: Do not paint a grey crown; that marks Lanius cristatus lucionensis, the Brown Shrike race that breeds in Korea.
Do not paint a duller brown crown, a narrow supercilium and little white on the forehead (nominate cristatus); superciliosus is the brightest rufous, with the widest white forehead.
Do not paint a large, obvious white wing patch (Bull-headed Shrike) or a grey crown with a black tail (Red-backed Shrike); at most a tiny white spot shows at the primary bases.
